name: New Hampshire
tagline: From moose country and White Mountain notches to Lake Winnipesaukee and the Seacoast.
intro: New Hampshire's byways climb through the notches of the White Mountains, run north into moose country and the paper-mill towns of the Androscoggin, circle Lake Winnipesaukee and Lake Sunapee, follow the Connecticut River, and wind through Shaker villages, orchards and colonial towns in the south before ending on a short stretch of Atlantic shore. This chapter follows the New Hampshire Scenic and Cultural Byways Program, set up in 1992 under RSA 238:19 and run by the New Hampshire Department of Transportation's Bureau of Planning and Community Assistance, and uses NHDOT's official byway map for the list. Many routes keep names like Trail or Tour from older tourism drives (the Currier & Ives began as a 1976 Bicentennial 'Yankee Trail'), and three of them, the Kancamagus, the White Mountains Trail and the Connecticut River Byway, are also National Scenic Byways.

programs.label: New Hampshire Scenic and Cultural Byways

members.name: American Independence Byway
members.blurb: A 21-mile loop joining Exeter and Hampton, two of the four towns New Hampshire began with, to Hampton Falls and Kensington, past open fields and salt marsh to an Exeter museum that holds a Dunlap broadside of the Declaration.

members.name: Apple Way
members.blurb: Londonderry's back roads wind past pick-your-own orchards, numbered district schoolhouses and the old sugar shack behind Dutton Farm's barn, ending on Mammoth Road at Mack's Orchards, a stop for apples and cider in the fall.

members.name: Branch River Valley Scenic Byway
members.blurb: NH 153 and NH 125 run through Wakefield and Milton toward the Maine line, by way of Wakefield Corner, a village with 26 buildings on the National Register, and the working nineteenth-century farm at the New Hampshire Farm Museum.

members.name: Coastal Byway
members.blurb: NH 1A keeps to the shore from Seabrook past the Hampton Beach boardwalk and the tidepools at Odiorne Point, then NH 1B swings around New Castle and its old harbor forts before ending in Portsmouth.

members.name: Connecticut River Byway
members.blurb: On the New Hampshire bank the byway follows NH 12A and NH 10 up the Connecticut, past the Cornish-Windsor covered bridge and the Saint-Gaudens home, through Hanover to Orford's row of Federal houses, the Seven Swans.

members.name: Currier and Ives Trail
members.blurb: Forty miles of Merrimack County farm roads between Daniel Webster's birthplace and the Franklin Pierce Homestead, past stone walls and hayfields with Mount Kearsarge on the skyline and two covered bridges in Hopkinton.

members.name: Enfield Shaker Village Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Three miles of NH 4A along the shore of Mascoma Lake, over the Shaker Bridge and past La Salette Shrine to the buildings and fields that once belonged to the Enfield Shaker community.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: General John Stark Byway
members.blurb: A loop on NH 13 and NH 77 through four small towns, named for the general credited with 'Live Free or Die', past farmland to Weare's 1837 town hall and New Boston's Molly Stark cannon.

members.name: Kancamagus Byway
members.blurb: NH 112 climbs out of Lincoln beside the East Branch of the Pemigewasset and the Hancock Branch, switchbacks over 2,855-foot Kancamagus Pass, then follows the Swift River down through national forest toward Conway.

members.name: Lake Sunapee Scenic & Cultural Byway
members.blurb: A 39-mile circuit of Lake Sunapee through the harbor villages of Sunapee and Newbury and the town of New London, catching the water between wooded hills on the way past The Fells and Mount Sunapee.

members.name: Lakes Region Tour
members.blurb: A long loop around Lake Winnipesaukee, from Alton Bay up NH 11 past Mount Major and the arcades of Weirs Beach to Meredith, then along the quieter eastern shore through Center Harbor and Moultonborough.

members.name: Mills Scenic Byway
members.blurb: NH 108 links the old mill towns of Newmarket and Durham, crossing the Lamprey and Oyster rivers beside dams and mill ponds, and the byway picks up again in Rollinsford among eighteenth-century farms near the Maine line.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Moose Path Trail
members.blurb: From Gorham the road follows the Androscoggin north through Berlin and the Thirteen Mile Woods to Errol, then crosses Dixville Notch past the Balsams and runs up US 3 into Pittsburg, where moose stand in roadside bogs.

members.name: Mountain Road Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 1.6-mile auto road, built in 1911, climbs Mount Prospect in Lancaster to the Weeks estate and its stone lookout tower, with views across the Presidential Range and the upper Connecticut River valley.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Old Stagecoach Scenic Byway
members.blurb: NH 121 follows the line of the old Boston-to-Concord stage road from Atkinson at the Massachusetts border north through Hampstead and Chester to the wooded shore of Massabesic Lake in Auburn.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Presidential Range Trail
members.blurb: A wide loop around the Presidentials from Littleton and Whitefield to Lancaster, east on US 2 beneath the northern peaks, down through Pinkham Notch, and back through Crawford Notch past the Mount Washington Hotel.

members.name: River Heritage Trail
members.blurb: A 120-mile loop from North Woodstock down to Plymouth, west under Mount Moosilauke to the Federal-era villages of Haverhill on the Connecticut, and home through Kinsman Notch past the long covered bridges at Bath and Woodsville.

members.name: Robert Frost Scenic Byway
members.blurb: In Derry the byway runs down NH 28 through the village to the farm where Robert Frost lived from 1900 to 1911, then wanders east on country roads to rejoin the old stage road in Hampstead.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Upper Lamprey Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A loop off NH 101 that roughly follows the upper Lamprey River through Candia's old mill village, Deerfield's farms and fairgrounds, and Northwood, known for the antique shops of its Antique Alley.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: White Mountains Trail
members.blurb: US 3 and US 302 thread Franconia Notch and Crawford Notch between Lincoln and Conway, closing the loop on the Kancamagus, with a side branch over Bear Notch and the Cog Railway's base road off 302 at Bretton Woods.

members.name: Woodland Heritage Trail
members.blurb: A 65-mile loop from Lancaster through the paper-mill village of Groveton and the covered bridge at Stark, down the Androscoggin past the 1936 Nansen Ski Jump to Berlin, and back on US 2 through Randolph and Jefferson.
